title: My Prompt - can you build a 3rd person view game in Unreal Engine entirely in c++? - The result
author: selfish_meme
selftext:
Claude Opus 5.5 reply (I thought I was asking a question if it was possible), I am already making a game in Unreal so already had Unreal setup and Visual studio it was simple to get running. I'm a little shocked, maybe everyone else isn't, but I am. Conversation Below.



can you build a 3rd person view game in Unreal Engine entirely in c++?

`Setting up the restart key and fall-off reset`

Yes. Unreal fully supports gameplay written only in C++, with no Blueprints. I’ve built you a small third-person game set up that way: you run around, climb a spiral of platforms and collect 14 glowing orbs against a timer.

`Created 17 files, shared a file, ran 2 commands`

I’ve built [**ThirdPersonCpp.zip**](http://ThirdPersonCpp.zip), a complete Unreal Engine 5 project written only in C++. I couldn’t compile it here because Unreal Engine can’t run in this workspace, so it hasn’t been built or played yet. Expect a few small fixes the first time it compiles.

The game is an orb collector: climb a spiral tower of platforms and search the ground to find 14 glowing orbs as fast as you can. A timer runs on screen, and you can restart with R.

**How “entirely in C++” works here:**

* **No Blueprints:** the game mode, character, pickups and HUD are all C++ classes, and the game mode is set in the config file.
* **No input assets:** the controls (keyboard, mouse and gamepad) are created in code when the game starts, using Unreal’s standard input system (Enhanced Input).
* **No saved level:** the game mode builds the whole world when the game starts: floor, sun and fill lights, sky, platforms, crates, orbs and the spawn point.
* **No imported art:** the character and orbs use the simple shapes that come with the engine, coloured in code.

**Running it:** unzip it, right-click the `.uproject` file and choose “Generate Visual Studio project files”, then open it. When it asks to build, say yes, then press Play. You need UE 5.3 or later plus Visual Studio 2022 or Xcode. The README has the controls and a map of the code.

**Caveat:** in practice, most real C++ Unreal games still use some editor-made assets, like animated characters and sounds. The usual approach is to keep all the logic in C++ and load assets from it. The README explains how to swap in the Mannequin character from Unreal’s Third Person template when you want a properly animated character.
